Not every item had a plan. The landed quick wins, ranks 18 (00ff0e7e), 19 (af9ba1fc), 20 (82095942), 43 (09fd911d/fba5af56), 57 (12ad5134), 58 (e578402d), 68 (0a8ed40a) and 70 (47799eb3), have no plan file. Each plan contains: (1) a first-hand verdict on the review claim, often correcting it — item 53 'panics every connection' was wrong in detail; item 13 'keyed RAW SSE' does not exist; item 14's SweepEviction cannot reach a feed engine; item 76's premise that the growth gate was red was stale. ADVERSARIAL DIFF REVIEW FOR HIGH-RISK FIXES. Bug #9 (668bc80c) and the registry descriptor cache (063a674d) each got 'three lenses and an adjudicator' on the first implementation. On bug #9 the review found a real regression: a declared closure names seg("") and never matched seg("gb"), which gave 503 'did not converge'. It was reproduced red before being fixed. The same review also required three more red-first cases: a fail-open refresh, a free sealed closure, and an incarnation fence. On the cache, the skeptic found an ABA in the first design (a cap purge between write and publish); it is pinned by a test with the cap set to two. Bug #4's design review found a third defect the original finding missed (a Receive's leases to other keys were dropped). Bug #6's review returned ten nits and no regression. RED-FIRST WITH CAPTURED OUTPUT. Every behavioural fix has a test that failed on the unfixed tree. The failure text is quoted in the commit message (e.g. 063a674d '1 passed; 4 failed'; 2fb92fb9 '1,686,963 reads in 503 ms'; 527d3d3a 'left: 200, right: 429'), and many are kept in scratchpad logs (b1..b8-red.log, red-27c1/27c2/32c1/32c2/35/65r1/65r2/69b.log). The reds were made deterministic: store decorators that run the concurrent writer inside the read's reply (registry cache), poisoned caches, per-name failpoints, paused or manual clocks, and bounded waits so a red fails in 5-20 s instead of hanging. Timing-sensitive greens were looped (e.g. 12/12, 8/8, 60/60). When the red has to be taken on an older commit while the main tree is busy, it is captured in a worktree that shares CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Some reds are compile-level only (the error codes quoted across the series are E0599, E0609, E0425, E0432, E0433 and E0061): a342ab6f, 74391f9c's unit tests, 6515a15d's unit tests, a0185c3b's monitor test and e19c80c5's postings_refusal_tests. Those prove an API was missing, not that behaviour was wrong. b9f3cd7c's exhaustiveness claim also rests on a compile-level probe: adding a cursor-verdict variant is E0004 (non-exhaustive patterns) at the scan page.

MUTATION TESTING BEFORE PUSH, FROM dd220be8 ON (CI's own selection, run locally). Setup: set QUALITY_EVENT_NAME=push, QUALITY_HEAD_SHA/QUALITY_BEFORE_SHA (previous pushed revision) and QUALITY_BASE_REF=origin/slate. Then run scripts/quality/verification_plan.py --out target/quality-plan, then scripts/quality/mutations.sh on the COMMITTED tree. Zero MISSED was required, because CI's mutation leg fails on any miss and has no disposition ledger. The retained logs show comparison_kind push-previous-revision and MUT_EXIT=0; for example mutations-b9.log has 50 mutants, 48 caught and 2 unviable. Survivors were killed with new tests (3dfb970f: the byte-capped arm in postings_cache load_runs). Equivalent mutants were restructured rather than excused: 063a674d (`within` with an explicit now), 5d60dc63 (a retry-wait table instead of 10*attempt), 61d03e34 (`|` -> `+` on disjoint offset fields; a redundant digit arm deleted; the `reversed` binding). Sometimes mutation went beyond CI's selection: mut-b9-own.log found the two `10 * attempt` survivors that led to 5d60dc63. New owners are killed whole-file at registration: 77c13d74 has offsets 37/37, telemetry_batch 25+1 unviable, and segmap, where 1 MISSED was fixed to 87+3 unviable. The practice did not exist for the first push. 7a6ecd23 was pushed at 14:37 +0700 on 09-21, and the earliest local plan/mutation log (scratchpad plan.log) is from 15:25, after that push. Its rust-quality mutation leg failed: the fleet row's filter `fleet::` reached no DST proofs. dd220be8 fixed the scope and, per its own message, re-ran CI's exact comparison locally only after rust-quality had failed (2/2 caught). Running CI's selection locally before each push began there. 7a6ecd23 is the only push whose CI mutation leg failed. No local mutation log was kept for batch 12 (a7f3167d+24c4c77a: a DST test module plus scripts/ci).

FULL LOCAL GATE ON MOST PUSHES. scripts/gate.sh writes to $OUT. It runs: (1) scripts/quality.sh: config check, actionlint, cargo fmt --check, the streams-quality-syntax crate tests, the Python unit tests (scripts/quality: 113 tests at the last gate, gate-b12, up from 101 at the start, gate-final), clippy -D warnings as JSON through the ratchet gate.py, rustdoc -D warnings with --document-private-items, cargo machete, cargo deny, every source gate's --self-test and --check, verify-rc-evidence --self-test, and the mt-lint leg. (2) `cargo test --release --lib` without the capacity test, checked by tests_ran.py against a floor derived from docs/refactor/test-inventory.json. (3) The capacity leg post_split_throughput_scales alone, with --exact, because it owns the machine. Gate and mutation runs were never run at the same time. The fast pre-flight was quality.sh (about 3 min). The local gate is narrower than CI: release --lib only, no bin or integration tests (item 69A says 66 are skipped), and no debug-assertions suite. Conformance (332/0/6) was re-run locally only for the TTL change efe12b2e; CI's conformance job covers every push. Retained evidence does not show a full gate for every push. Four tooling pushes on 09-23 (0a8ed40a, 47799eb3, 09fd911d and fba5af56, pushed 11:05-11:23 +0700) have only quality.sh logs (quality-r68/r70/r43) and no gate file. ROOT-CAUSING CI FAILURES INSTEAD OF RETRYING. F-G, the dst livefeed_owner_movement_one_redirect_and_typed_cutoffs hang, happened twice on CI and never locally (25+60 isolated runs, 4 parallel suites). It was handled in stages. First, the only unbounded fixture waits were bounded (d8689572; they did not fire on the recurrence). Then a stack-dump watchdog was added to CI (4c51ebfd). Then a same-thread deadlock was identified by reading the code and reproduced deterministically in a synthesized test: TaskSupervisor::spawn holds its std mutex across tokio::spawn; a closing runtime drops the refused future inside that call; the RequiredExit guard's drop then re-locks the same mutex. The fix is 714abcc2 (tasks/refusal.rs). The vacuous assertion in dst runtime_isolation (9b2f53bc) was found by running the full suite after item 57 (12ad5134) made fleet append errors visible. No cloud, staging or field runs were part of this program.
gate_traps: The gate needs Python >= 3.11 (tomllib) but calls bare `python3`; the stock macOS 3.9 dies. Put a shim directory first on PATH with python3 -> /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12. docs/RUST-QUALITY.md is normative (AGENTS.md points to it).
gate.sh writes its report to $OUT (environment variable, default /tmp/gate.txt), NOT to $1. It is fail-closed per stage: GATEFAIL-quality, -suite, -suite-ran, -capacity, -capacity-ran, then GATEDONE.

Files over 1,000 lines may not grow by ONE line compared with the push base. These include fleet.rs, history.rs, shard.rs, product.rs, http.rs, registry.rs, auth.rs, billing.rs and sse/feed.rs. DST test files are ALSO ceilinged: split them into a new #[path] module, add an owners.json by-path row and a src/dst/tests/README.md entry, and widen any mutation filter that named the old module (d93b421b created livefeed_engine_retired.rs for this reason). Doc edits must be line-neutral, or code must move out first in a pure verbatim-move commit. The next merge base lowers the ceiling to the new size.

A function-wide unwrap_used/expect_used #[expect] fingerprints EVERY path-call under it, so changing one call counts as 'accepted exception grew'. Scopes also ratchet scope_lines and syntax_facts. The ways out are: narrow the exception (move code out of the scope, as e6550142 did), or re-decide its reason text, which gives it a new identity. A tokio::spawn(async move {..}) under such a scope is ONE fingerprinted call-site and cannot be edited in place (spawn_load in d2e87129, the feed retry task in d902a85b, get_or_open's reaper in fd810688).

Fingerprints resolve import aliases. MOVING a callee to a new module changes the fingerprint of every ratcheted caller even when the caller's text is untouched (product_entry after product_scan moved). A verbatim-move commit can therefore fail the gate on its own: push it paired with the fix that re-decides the reasons, and say so in the message. A call through an absolute path does not move (fc18a704 re-exported spawn_telemetry). Keep types that ratcheted scopes name in place (CachedDesc stayed in registry.rs in ca36a7f4).

After DELETING an exception, run `gate.py --prune`; it needs a successful clippy build first. An unfulfilled #[expect] is denied, so shrinking a function under 100 lines forces deletion of its too_many_lines expectation (74391f9c, 796211d7, 6ef3bc64). The architecture gate now refuses obsolete budget exceptions (47799eb3): shrinking a function below its baseline makes its budget exception mandatory to delete (fb18840d, 6515a15d).

CI's mutation leg FAILS on ANY missed mutant (cargo-mutants exit 2, driver check=True) and has no disposition ledger. An equivalent mutant (e.g. `<` vs `<=` on elapsed()<ttl, `|` vs `^` on disjoint bit fields, `rate > 0.0` vs `>= 0.0`) must be made killable, for example by extracting the predicate with an explicit `now`, or the code must be restructured or the redundant condition deleted. It cannot be tested around. cargo-mutants reports a hung test as TIMEOUT, which does not count as detection, so every await in a test must be bounded (5c306651).

New files under critical prefixes (src/sse, src/postings*, the src/fleet.rs scope, src/http) need a row in scripts/quality/mutation_owners.py, test files included. An owner whose test filter matches 0 tests leaves every mutant MISSED in CI (rust-quality), and you only see that locally if you run the plan; this is what failed 7a6ecd23, fixed by dd220be8. A registered owner row makes CI mutation-test that file on EVERY change even outside CRITICAL_PREFIXES (`p in by_source`).

Mutation owner filters are OR'ed libtest substrings passed as `cargo test <f0> -- <f1> ...`. A DST test runs in the leg only if its module path contains a filter, e.g. `dst_tests::read_application::`. `http::read::` matches nothing, because the module is `http::read_adapter`.

Before EVERY push, run CI's own selection: QUALITY_EVENT_NAME=push, QUALITY_HEAD_SHA, QUALITY_BEFORE_SHA (the previous pushed revision), QUALITY_BASE_REF=origin/slate, then `scripts/quality/verification_plan.py --out target/quality-plan`. If mutants are selected, run scripts/quality/mutations.sh; the change must be COMMITTED. Since 24c4c77a, merge_base() refuses a push event without QUALITY_BEFORE_SHA. Before that, ci.yml's architecture-report compared HEAD with HEAD on every push.

Each owner's cargo-mutants run copies the tree when THAT owner starts. In a multi-owner mutations.sh run, editing the main tree mid-run therefore contaminates later owners. Never edit during mutations.sh, and never during gate.sh.
Never run the gate and a mutation leg at the same time. CPU contention depresses the capacity leg (post_split_throughput_scales owns the machine) and can make mutants TIMEOUT.

docs/quality/owners.json needs reasoned rows for macro-dsl uses (proptest!, json!, tokio::select!), unresolved globs (`use super::*` in a new test file), by-path #[path] modules, effect owners (tokio::spawn, JoinSet::spawn, thread_local, detached threads), and statics. These rows MOVE with the code: add the new path, drop the vacated source-allowances.json row (prune does this; hand-edit when prune refuses because another finding stands). Never re-sort owners.json; insert in place.

JSON ledgers use different encodings: test-scenario-map and scenario-dispositions are written with ensure_ascii=True, owners.json with ensure_ascii=False. Round-trip HEAD before rewriting any JSON ledger.

After changing a DST test body, run `python3 scripts/test-inventory.py --write` and check that the diff contains only the intended hashes. If the test is pinned, hand-edit its sha256 in docs/refactor/review-mechanisms.json (and test-additions.json). function_hash masks comments.

clippy in tests: allowances only under an EXACT #[cfg(test)]. The nesting limit of 4 applies to tests too, so extract a helper. rustfmt re-blocks a too-long match arm, which can trip the nesting limit: shorten names or use a helper fn. SAFETY comments sit on the statement that holds the unsafe block. Environment reads go only through config::ProcessEnvironment; a342ab6f removed the last production read outside it.

Gate legs must prove they ran (00ff0e7e: scripts/test-leg.sh + scripts/quality/tests_ran.py). `cargo test <filter>` exits 0 with 'ok. 0 passed' when nothing matches. Renaming a --exact test, or shrinking the inventory, moves the floors.

A comment-only edit inside a function body still selects that function's whole-body mutant (the in-diff span overlaps). Doc comments outside the body do not. The same applies to a `///` added under a function-wide ratcheted scope: it adds fingerprinted path facts (fb18840d used plain comments instead).
Making a swallowed error visible can turn a vacuous assertion red somewhere else (item 57 -> runtime_isolation, 9b2f53bc). Run the FULL suite (the gate) before pushing even a 'small' fail-open fix.

The lib tests run as ONE process in CI. Process statics (POSTINGS_BYTES_WRITTEN, READ_FRAMES_MATCHED, LEASE_TERMINATIONS, and the former OpenGate statics) are shared with every concurrently running test, so assert per-engine or per-runtime state (0aaa1ef1, a1cf29f3). Registry failpoints are keyed by (point, stream name): isolate with a unique stream name rather than gap_lock (a4de4f51, 29ff93c4).

libtest prints a test's panic only after the test function returns, and that includes the tokio runtime drop, which joins workers with no timeout. A hang during runtime teardown therefore prints nothing. CI now has scripts/quality/hang_dump.sh (4c51ebfd): after 15 minutes it dumps gdb stacks of the lib test binary and kills it.

Removing a method from a type that Derefs to another type can compile silently through the deref target's method of the same name (StreamDesc -> PersistedDescriptor::epoch_bytes, 796211d7). Delete both.

The multitenancy audit (scripts/multitenancy-audit.sh) now scans every src/**/*.rs and fails on GONE rows as well as NEW ones (09fd911d). A move or conversion must regenerate scripts/mt-audit-baseline.txt in its own reviewed diff; it went 67 -> 77 -> 78 rows. Use `[ \t]`, not `[[:space:]]`: CI's mawk does not support POSIX classes (fba5af56).

Rig routing: one shard prefix, "00". `_audit_events` hashes to "00" and is owned by whoever holds it. `_ops_events`, `_usage` and `_ops_metrics` fall back to the empty prefix "", whose rendezvous owner is rig-a. Use `_audit_events` for a 'non-owner' system-append test on rig-b.

`gh run list --branch slate` without createdAt once surfaced runs from an older push. Always include createdAt and headSha and match the sha. Never claim green from memory. `gh run list` shows the latest attempt only, so a re-run hides the first failure (5c0e62d6).

CI runners are about 4x slower than local. rust-quality with item 55's 20 shard mutants took 2h04m, against a 240-minute invariant-tools deadline (af9ba1fc). CI job deadlines were set at 2x or more the observed maximum over 40 green runs.

Loom 0.7.2 treats SeqCst as AcqRel, so a plain SeqCst store still fails a store-buffering model. Only RMWs (swap/CAS) pass it (aaf2baa5). The repo's Loom models run inside the ordinary test build and Loom atomics panic outside a model, so the atomic type cannot switch on cfg(test); make the owner generic over the word (SweepCustody<W: CustodyWord>).

Workflow-designed plans are good but not authoritative. Their controls are sometimes unbuildable (enforce mode cannot create a stream in the deployment tenant, 84f80b75), they omit ledger rows, and skeptic claims can be wrong (redundant_clone on `.segments.clone()` through Deref does not fire). Check first-hand.

F-G (714abcc2): is tasks/refusal.rs the right fix? It is a thread_local slot that sets aside a future dropped inside tokio::spawn by a closing runtime and drops it after the registration mutex is released. The alternative is to restructure TaskSupervisor::spawn so tokio::spawn never runs under that std mutex (e.g. reserve the registration, release the lock, spawn, then settle). Is the evidence enough to call the CI hang root-caused? The evidence is: a synthesized deterministic red (a_spawn_refused_by_a_closing_runtime_cannot_deadlock_its_supervisor); the original DST test never hung locally in 85+ runs; the hang struck twice in about 43 pushes, and 7 pushes have been green since.

Wire changes that shipped and were reported to the owner only after the fact (the full list). Are they acceptable to the SDK and to clients? The list: 413 payload_too_large/body_too_large for a record count over a fresh bucket (was 429 with retry-after: 1 forever); :scan and consumer :pull gaining 429 project_rate_limit, plus Cache-Control: no-store on :pull; /v1/debug answering 401 instead of 404/405 for unrouted paths or wrong methods without the token; telemetry-append relays now allowed up to MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES (32 MiB, ~2x per concurrent relay), with unauthenticated uploads getting 401 unread; extend visibilityMs:0 floored to 1 s; Stream-TTL ceiling 2^32-1 s (400 above it); h1 header/idle deadline defaulting to 120 s (never measured against the platform edge's upstream pool idle, F-E); 409 not_ring_owner (not 404) from the relay receiver; 503 temporarily_unavailable (not 404) from internal receivers on a registry fault; watch waits on a non-owner answering 409 with Streams-Replay-To; a lease on a project placed on another cell ending as 403 project_missing, not the request path's 421 wrong_cell (1791207a); /health applying the billing gate for argv-configured deployments (46d4b7df). Three pending decisions touch the same surface. (a) Producer-Id length (found while planning item 53): an id of 65,503 bytes or more makes the producer key exceed slatedb's u16 key limit, and WriteBatch::put panics inside the committer. The plan says this is reachable when SSE_H1_MAX_BUF is raised, and possibly at the 64 KiB default, because hyper's max_buf_size is a soft threshold. Should it be fixed now with a length check in parse_producer answered by the existing 400 invalid_producer, and at what limit? (b) Item 88 step 2: refusing four kinds of non-canonical offset token is a new 400 on raw reads, SSE, internal segment reads and forks. (c) The offset encoder drops epoch bits 30-31, so segment 2^30+k's tokens collide with segment k's; the recommendation is to cap segment-id allocation at 2^30 (no wire change).

Capacity leg flake and the unexplained 500. Batch 12's local gate failed at the capacity leg: dst::dst_tests::topology_scaling::post_split_throughput_scales panicked with 'append during capacity run: 500' at 8.63 s (scratchpad gate-b12.txt.capacity.log). origin/slate's reflog shows 24c4c77a pushed at 08:36:38 +0700, about 90 s after that gate file was last written. In between, three isolated re-runs of the capacity leg passed; no production code had changed since the previous green gate. The reproduction attempts (cap-loop.sh, cap-stress.sh, cap-tally.log) came after the push. The failure did not reproduce: 60/60 isolated runs green; 40 runs under 8 busy cores and further runs under 16 busy cores produced only a different, benign failure, the single-shot 'split executes' decline (2 of the 40). Since bc43a2bb the capacity leg runs under the shipped absorber posture (effective budget 100,859,904 bytes, 2 slots, effective concurrency 1); gates b7 through b11 passed under it. The suspects are a write racing a closing store reported as 500 internal (item 47) and ResolveError::OpenFailed mapping to 500. Both are unfixed. CI was green on 24c4c77a.

F-G is 'likely' root-caused, not proven. The original hang (dst livefeed_ownership::livefeed_owner_movement_one_redirect_and_typed_cutoffs; CI runs on 82095942 and 33fbd10e, run 35870075157) never reproduced locally. The deterministic red is a synthesized current-thread-runtime scenario that shows the deadlock shape exists, not that it was the cause. The base rate was 2 hangs in about 43 pushes, and only 7 pushes (714abcc2 through 24c4c77a) have been green since the fix, which is weak statistical evidence. The fix (tasks/refusal.rs) relies on a thread_local set-aside of futures dropped inside tokio::spawn, which is subtle. If the hang recurs, hang_dump.sh (4c51ebfd) should print the stuck stacks within 15 minutes. Before the fix, a production shutdown could deadlock the same way.
